source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
Anthracnose stalk rot (ជម្ងឺពុកដើម, Anthracnose): at the tasseling stage of corn, farmers may observe that the stem begins to develop soft rot, with visible lesions on the stem and leaf sheath that appear water-soaked at first. Diseased fields show scattered rotted stems throughout. Leaf spots appear diamond-shaped along the leaf, following the leaf veins. This disease is caused by fungal spores that spread within the field when there is standing water or moisture and wind. This disease is favored by conditions where the atmosphere is warm and humid, especially cloudy weather before rain.

To control this disease, farmers should scout the crop and remove infected debris promptly and dispose of it away from the field, and clear/collect stem residues so it does not carry over as inoculum for the following crop. Before planting, seed should be soaked/treated with a fungicide such as Mancozeb at about a 2% concentration, and if lesion symptoms of this disease are found during growth, spray a fungicide at the recommended concentration, about every 7 days.
